completion.text: {"insufficient_evidence": false, "answer": "The airplane veered left off the runway because the left main gear spring assembly separated from the underside of the fuselage during the takeoff roll. [20230921193112:factual] The assembly failed due to fatigue cracking and overload stresses, with the fatigue crack likely initiated by corrosion under the primer paint and inside the dimples of the shot-peened area. [20230921193112:analysis] The corrosion was likely present before the zinc-rich primer was applied in March 2010, and its inadequate removal allowed the crack to propagate until overstress failure. [20230921193112:analysis] The NTSB determined the probable cause was the failure of the left main landing gear spring assembly due to a fatigue crack, with improper maintenance that allowed corrosion to develop contributing.
